newEvidence: Bend’s proof and execution results are backed by the dedicated runtime review. The Kujo side now also has executed Spec, Eval and RunLedger controls, plus a Linux Workcell Docker fixture. Bend GPU execution, parallel speedup and a direct Kujo–Bend adapter remain outside this review.

The 20261019.a nightly and matching Python bridge reproduced all 32 prior boundary outcomes, including the invalid-integer arithmetic crash. Hosted model quality, cloud trace delivery and other language bridges remain outside these local fixtures. The upstream issue remains the place to follow maintainer status.

The extended merge test executed both independent edits: main printed the edited text, and a generated test confirmed that the merged arithmetic returned 38 for 40 and 2. The 55 command observations include the earlier refresh, conflict and rollback controls. Concurrent writers, power-loss recovery and complex multi-file merges remain untested.

The direct comparisons now link runtime evidence for Bend, BAML and Zerolang. The Kujo workflow claims also have positive and negative Spec/Eval fixtures, RunLedger and Fence contract tests, and a Linux Workcell Docker run. Python, TypeScript and Rust remain documented alternatives; this guide makes no measured productivity or performance ranking.

Agents SDK passed six budget and 32 runner contract tests, including cancellation, timeout, retry and approval-denial cases with offline callbacks. Dispatch completed an offline workflow and recognized it as already completed on resume. Watchdog’s loopback proxy suite passed. Workcell ran Docker success/failure and receipt-integrity controls on Linux with Kujo 1.6.0. These cases do not establish live-provider reliability, interrupted external-effect recovery or general deployment security.

Spec accepted a valid task record and rejected a missing goal. Eval accepted the expected JSON value and rejected a different expected value. Fence passed 317 upstream assertions; RunLedger passed 81 unit assertions and its CLI suite. ShipCheck’s gate passed a repository containing a test that exited 7 when run separately: test presence is not test execution.

The public exercise accepted the correct artifact and rejected wrong-value, malformed and wrong-type controls. A separate producer printed correct JSON but exited 7; the exercise correctly failed. Kujo 1.8.0 was rejected by the 1.8.2 version gate. Workcell also accepted an intact Docker run receipt and rejected a modified log. Revision matching and application-specific acceptance criteria remain the reviewer’s responsibility.
